title: Eleven Rows and One Frame
subtitle: 蔬菜与种植 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 蔬菜与种植（生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：蔬菜与种植（生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：cucumber　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cucumber 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my grandmother ① grew a cucumber that reached eleven inches in a cold frame, and she said the growing was the whole of the summer. The ② cucumber, meaning the vegetable and not the plant, was cut on a Sunday and stayed that crisp; cucumber, she said, is the only thing in a frame that is judged by how quickly it is eaten.

Every ③ cucumber in that frame had the same pale stripe, and the ④ cucumber at the end, meaning the one she kept for the show and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever measured twice. Cucumber, my mother said, is nine parts stripe and one part somebody willing to cut it; my grandmother said the cutting is the part that fills the summer.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the cucumber was the whole of the sandwich, meaning the slice and not the vegetable. The ⑥ cucumber, meaning the slice and not any of that, is the only thing in a sandwich that everybody asks for and nobody tastes; cucumber, he said, is either something you grow or the only word that means both a vegetable and a slice. She said the slice is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ cucumber had become a line in a show schedule, and the schedule had become an argument about the stripe. The ⑧ cucumber of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in July, was one frame and thirty years of cutting; cucumber, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to cut it. He said the cutting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cucumber I remember is the one at the end, which she cut in 1967 and is still described as the straightest in the county. A ⑩ cucumber, my mother said in 1969, is the only thing that improves by being eaten; every cucumber, she said, is a slice that has agreed to look like a vegetable. She said the slice was the honest half.

answers.why: grow a cucumber 意为“种黄瓜”，1953 年祖母在一个冷床里种出了一条长到十一英寸的黄瓜。
cucumber 意为“黄瓜”，指那条瓜本身而不是那株藤，它在一个星期天被摘下。
cucumber 指那个温床里每一条黄瓜，每一条都有同样的浅色条纹。
cucumber 指末尾那一条（她留给展览的那一条），是唯一有人量过两次的。
cucumber 意为“黄瓜片”，父亲说那片黄瓜就是那份三明治的全部，指的是夹在里面的薄片而不是那条瓜。
cucumber 为转喻用法，指三明治里的那一片而不是那条瓜，是三明治里人人都要求加、却无人尝出味道的东西。
cucumber 意为“黄瓜”，指展览日程表上提到的那一条，到 1961 年这条黄瓜成了日程表里的一行。
cucumber 意为“黄瓜”，祖母七月写道，整件事的黄瓜是一个温床三十年的采摘。
cucumber 意为“黄瓜”，我记得的是末尾那一条，她 1967 年摘下，至今仍被说成全县最直的。
cucumber 为抽象总称，母亲说一条黄瓜是唯一会因为被吃掉而变好的东西。
